events.fact: Google OAuth registration console is the Google Cloud Console (console.cloud.google.com), where developers create a project, configure the OAuth consent screen (App type: Internal or External), and create OAuth client ID credentials (application type: Web application).

Google OAuth verification requirements for production: External apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes must complete Google OAuth verification. This includes brand verification (domain verification in Search Console, privacy policy, home page, branding page) and sensitive/restricted scope verification (submitting a detailed scope justification and an unlisted YouTube demo video showing the end-to-end OAuth flow and scope usage).

Google restricted scopes (such as gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.basic, and mail.google.com) carry strict requirements. If restricted data is stored or transmitted via a third-party server, an annual security assessment via the Cloud Application Security Assessment (CASA) framework by an authorized third-party lab (costing $500–$4,500, taking 2–6 weeks) is mandatory upon Google request.

Development-mode / unverified app limits: Unverified apps in 'Testing' mode have a cap of 100 test users, and refresh tokens expire after 7 days if the app is unverified or in testing status. Unverified apps also trigger a prominent full-page warning screen ("Access blocked: App hasn't been verified") for arbitrary external users.

Gmail API quotas and rate limits: Free standard use provides 1,200,000 quota units per minute per project and 6,000 quota units per minute per user per project, with a daily cap of 80,000,000 quota units per project.

Typical Gmail agent scopes include sensitive and restricted scopes like https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send, and https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.compose.

Google OAuth technical details: Authorization endpoint is https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth, token endpoint is https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, and PKCE (methods plain, S256) is fully supported.

events.fact: Google OAuth verification timelines (official vs real world): Officially, brand verification takes 2–3 business days, sensitive scope verification takes 3–10 business days, and restricted scope verification can take up to 6 weeks. Real-world community reports frequently indicate reviews stalling for 8–10 weeks if actions/responses are missed or queues are backed up.

Gmail API usage limits & quotas: Standard free tier provides 1,200,000 quota units per minute per project, 6,000 quota units per minute per user per project, and 80,000,000 quota units per day per project. Standard use is free, with planned billing for daily usage exceeding threshold units starting late 2026. Exponential backoff with random jitter is required for HTTP 429 errors.
